fullPassage: Curiously, it became rather trendy in the late 20th century to claim to know nothing about science or mathematics. There was a popular belief that scientific knowledge was somehow at odds with being a cultured individual, when in fact it is central to it. In 1959, the English scientist and novelist C. P. Snow delivered a famous lecture in which he spoke of the distance and even animosity that existed between the 'two cultures' of science and the arts, or humanities. This deep division in intellectual life was, he felt, holding up human progress. The divide remained, and even increased, in the following decades. It might now be narrowing, but it's far from closed. More people, though, now recognize that knowing about science is not a mark of philistinism, but the very opposite. An informed appreciation of the world around us, the laws it follows and how we can discover those laws, puts us in the best position to make the most of our individual lives and the resources the planet affords us as a species. The loss of wild places was mourned poetically by 19th-century writers such as Wordsworth or Thoreau and demonstrated a need to find out how to renew and protect the environment. But this deep regret for what humans have done to the world, invoked through the arts, can be used in helpful action through the application of science and understanding.

det.analysis: 본문 9문장에 'The loss of wild places was mourned poetically ~ and demonstrated a need to find out how to renew and protect the environment'라고 명시되어 있으므로, '알아내야 할 방법'에 해당하는 표현은 'how to renew and protect the environment'(환경을 회복하고 보호하는 방법, 7단어)이다. stem의 '환경을 되살리고 지키는 방법'은 'how to renew and protect the environment'의 패러프레이즈이다.
det.tip: 'how to V'는 '~하는 방법'이라는 의미의 명사구입니다. renew(회복하다)와 protect(보호하다)가 and로 병렬 연결되어 the environment를 공유합니다.

accept: how to renew and protect the environment

questions.passage: Curiously, it became rather trendy in the late 20th century to claim to know nothing about science or mathematics. There was a popular belief that scientific knowledge was somehow at odds with being a cultured individual, when in fact it is central to it. In 1959, the English scientist and novelist C. P. Snow delivered a famous lecture in which he spoke of the distance and even animosity that existed between the 'two cultures' of science and the arts, or humanities. This deep division in intellectual life was, he felt, holding up human progress. The divide remained, and even increased, in the following decades. It might now be narrowing, but it's far from closed. More people, though, now recognize that knowing about science is not a mark of philistinism, but the very opposite. An informed appreciation of the world around us, the laws it follows and how we can discover those laws, puts us in the best position to make the most of our individual lives and the resources the planet affords us as a species. The loss of wild places was mourned poetically by 19th-century writers such as Wordsworth or Thoreau and demonstrated a need to find out how to renew and protect the environment. But this deep regret for what humans have done to the world, invoked through the arts, can be used in helpful action through the application of science and understanding.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 예술을 통해 환기된 세상에 대한 깊은 유감이 전환될 수 있는 결과를 나타내는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로, 9단어)

det.korean: 본문 10문장에서 후회가 전환될 수 있는 것은 'helpful action through the application of science and understanding'(과학과 이해의 적용을 통한 유용한 행동)입니다.
det.analysis: 본문 10문장에 'this deep regret ~ can be used in helpful action through the application of science and understanding'이라고 명시되어 있으므로, 후회가 전환되는 결과는 'helpful action through the application of science and understanding'이다. stem의 '과학의 적용을 통해 전환될 수 있는 것'은 'can be used in helpful action through the application of'의 패러프레이즈이다.
det.tip: 'through the application of ~'는 '~의 적용/응용을 통하여'라는 의미의 전치사구입니다. 예술이 문제의식을 환기하고, 과학이 그것을 실질적 행동으로 전환한다는 것이 글의 결론입니다.

questions.wa: helpful action through the application of science and understanding
accept: helpful action through the application of science and understanding

P. Snow discussed the distance and even animosity that existed between the two cultures of science and the arts in his 1959 lecture.'
det.tip: 'animosity'는 '적대감, 증오심'을 뜻하는 명사로, distance(거리)보다 더 강한 감정적 표현입니다. 'even'은 '심지어'라는 부사로, 단순한 거리를 넘어 적대감까지 있었음을 강조합니다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 맞게 영작하시오. (영어로)
"사실 그것은 그것에 핵심적이다"
[조건] (1) central, fact, in, is, it, it, to를 모두 사용
(2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 사실 그것은 그것에 핵심적이다
det.analysis: 'in fact it is central to it'은 'in fact(사실) + it(그것은) + is(~이다) + central(핵심적인) + to it(그것에)'의 구조이다. 부사구 in fact이 문두에서 역접을 만들고, it is central to it에서 두 개의 it은 각각 scientific knowledge와 being a cultured individual을 가리킨다.
det.tip: 'in fact'은 '사실은'이라는 뜻으로 앞선 내용을 반박할 때 쓰입니다. 'central to ~'는 '~에 핵심적인'이라는 뜻의 형용사구입니다.

questions.wa: in fact it is central to it
accept: in fact it is central to it

[조건] (1) a, about, is, knowing, mark, not, of, philistinism, science를 모두 사용

det.tip: 동명사구(knowing about science)가 주어로 쓰이면 단수 취급하여 is를 씁니다. 'a mark of ~'는 '~의 표시/징표'라는 뜻입니다.
